subject: Integrations: BrightLayer webhook failures — on-call ownership & runbook handoff
messages:
From: BrightLayer Support <support@brightlayer.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Nick O'Reilly <nick@cloudsona.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Webhook delivery failures to redwood-inference / 5xx responses

Hi Marissa / Mateo,

We started seeing a spike of failed webhook deliveries to Redwood endpoints (POST /v1/integrations/brightlayer/webhook) starting ~08:55 PDT. Payloads are getting 5xx from the edge layer with intermittent 502/504. Attached is the latest sample payload batch and short syslog excerpt (brightlayer_payloads_0914.log).

Impact: ~12 failed deliveries in last 15 minutes for multiple customers; CloudSona reported retries affecting fanout.

What we've tried: retries (our side), lowering concurrency from 8->2, switching to HTTP/1.1 — failures persist.

Asking: can you confirm who owns the on-call for the edge gateway and whether Redwood can change routing to the fallback endpoint while you triage? Also attaching a Zendesk ticket: https://redwood.zendesk.com/tickets/78934.

Ellen Park
Integration Lead, BrightLayer Consulting
ellen.park@brightlayer.io

Attachments: brightlayer_payloads_0914.log (text/log, 87KB)

Thanks for the flag, Ellen — and sorry you're seeing this. Mateo, we're looping you since BrightLayer is seeing backend edge errors.

- I'm opening a PagerDuty escalation to the edge/backend on-call now (PD incident linked below).
- Mateo/dylan: can you confirm whether the redirection/fallback route (us-west-fallback.redwood.ai) can be enabled for BrightLayer while we triage? That would buy uptime for affected customers.

Ellen: we'll keep CloudSona and your SRE updated in-thread. If the fallback is viable, please coordinate with us on a short maintenance window to validate.

Date: 2027-09-14T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: AS-NEEDS: BrightLayer webhook failures — triage request + runbook link

Hello on-call team,

BrightLayer is reporting persistent 5xx responses from our edge when they POST webhooks to /v1/integrations/brightlayer/webhook. They attached payload samples (see brightlayer_payloads_0914.log). Impacting partner BrightLayer customers, specifically CloudSona (see Nick O'Reilly CC'd).

Please triage and confirm:
- whether the edge gateway is returning 502/504 due to upstream timeouts or TLS failures
- whether a temporary routing to us-west-fallback.redwood.ai is possible for the partner tenant
- an ETA for a mitigation, and any recommended customer-facing text we can share with CloudSona/BrightLayer

Link to runbook + previous integration notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B7-brightlayer-integration-runbook

Attachments: brightlayer_payloads_0914.log

Thanks — Marissa
(automated escalation opened PD-123456)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: engineering-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AS-NEEDS: BrightLayer webhook failures — triage request + runbook link

On Thu, Sep 14, 2027 at 09:40, marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> BrightLayer is reporting persistent 5xx responses from our edge when they POST webhooks...

Quick update from triage: root cause appears to be a TLS session renegotiation issue between BrightLayer's HTTP/2 client and our edge (rls-edge). The edge is intermittently dropping the connection during ALPN/HTTP2 frames which propagates as 502/504 to the client. Reproducer: we replayed the payloads in brightlayer_payloads_0914.log with a test client configured for HTTP/2 and saw identical 502s starting at ~350ms into the stream.

Temporary mitigation applied (10:02):
- disabled HTTP/2 for brightlayer tenant at the proxy layer (fall back to HTTP/1.1) — this reduced failures immediately in our test harness.
- increased upstream keepalive timeout to 60s to reduce premature TCP teardown.

Planned fix:
- deploy a small edge patch to the rls-edge TLS handshake path that addresses a race condition (patch attached: rls_edge_patch_notes.diff). I expect the patch to land to canary in ~3 hours and full rollout in ~6–8 hours if all looks good.

Customer-facing text (suggestion):
"We identified an intermittent TLS handshaking issue between BrightLayer's client and our edge gateway that caused 5xx responses. We've applied a temporary routing change and will deploy a fix today; no customer data loss is expected. We will follow up when the patch is fully rolled out."

I'll keep this thread updated and will post the canary link once deployed.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rls_edge_patch_notes.diff

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightlayer.io>, support@brightlayer.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-14T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integrations: BrightLayer webhook failures — on-call ownership & runbook handoff

Ellen / BrightLayer team — thanks for patience and for the payload samples. Dylan's mitigation successfully stopped the 5xx spike earlier this afternoon; our canary shows stable delivery after the HTTP/2 disable and the edge patch rollout.

Next steps:
- We'll keep HTTP/2 disabled for 24 hours while we monitor telemetry.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute runbook review next Tue 09/21 to walk through the webhook health checks and make the fallback route a documented option in the BrightLayer runbook? Agenda: ownership, PagerDuty routing, fallback endpoint playbook, and API client recommendations (HTTP/1.1 fallback).
- I'll upload the final runbook draft to the shared Drive folder and drop the Zendesk resolution note.

Public summary you can share with customers:
"On 2027-09-14 we observed intermittent delivery failures for BrightLayer webhooks caused by TLS/HTTP2 handshaking mismatches with the Redwood edge. Temporary routing and an edge patch were implemented; services are restored and we will monitor for 24 hours. A joint runbook review is scheduled to prevent recurrence."

Attachments: brightlayer_runbook_v1.2.pdf

Thanks — Mateo
